implementation_notes: Use LINQ where it reads as a sentence, records for named data, and `var` when the type is obvious from the right-hand side. Nullable reference types (`string?`) make intent explicit. Avoid `Func<>` chains that read worse than a named local function.
idiom_name: LINQ as sentences + records + nullable annotations
code_sketch:
var payable = orders.Where(o => o.IsDue).Sum(o => o.Total);   // reads as the rule
public string? MiddleName { get; init; }   // nullability is intent
pitfalls: Async void, which hides the fact that a method is asynchronous at all
